excerpt: Cue by Manus gives each personal AI agent its own phone number, email address, payment card and computer to handle everyday tasks. What it does, how to get it and what launch-day users asked.
content:
Cue is a personal-agent app from Manus, the company behind the Manus general AI agent. Each agent you create gets its own identity: a phone number to make and take calls and send messages, an email address, a wallet that pays with permissions you set, and a dedicated computer workspace. Cue says agents take the calls you forward to them and keep working after you log off. You can also bring several agents into one group chat to work together, for example on a trip itinerary, packing list and bookings.

The examples on its site are household admin: booking a pediatrician or flu shot, emailing a hotel about connecting rooms, finding urgent care that takes a given insurer, or booking a Taskrabbit tasker. Apps are offered for macOS, Windows and mobile. One Product Hunt commenter reported that the app needed an invite code at launch.

Cue launched on Product Hunt on 2 October 2026 and finished #11 for the day with 108 points and 4 comments (as of 14 October 2026).

We have not tested Cue ourselves. Giving an AI agent a phone number and a payment card means trusting it with real money and real conversations, so check its permission settings carefully. This page brings together Cue's official site, its Product Hunt page and the public pages of the products it is compared with, and says where each fact comes from.

fit: spend a lot of time on calls, emails and bookings for a household and want to hand them off
want an assistant that can phone a clinic or email a hotel on your behalf rather than only drafting messages
are comfortable setting and reviewing permissions for payments
not_fit: can't get an invite: a Product Hunt commenter reported needing an invite code at launch
need published pricing before you start: we found none on cue.im
are uneasy about an AI making payments: commenters asked whether permissions are granted once or per transaction, and we found no public answer

pricing.intro: Pricing not published on cue.im as of 14 October 2026. Product Hunt lists Cue as having free options.
notes: Cue's legal terms and privacy policy are those of Manus (manus.im).

alternatives.intro: These are products Product Hunt lists as alternatives. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own.

items.name: Pally
items.what: Personal assistant you use over text messages
items.difference: You text one assistant. Cue gives each agent its own phone number, email, wallet and computer.

items.name: Lindy
items.difference: Aimed at work and business workflows; Cue's examples are personal and family admin.

items.name: BetterClaw
items.what: Hosted platform to deploy an AI agent
items.difference: Bring-your-own-key agent hosting for technical users rather than a consumer app with built-in phone and payments.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Martin (4.57 from 7 reviews) and Ace from Automat Workforce.

faq.a: An app from Manus for personal AI agents. Each agent has its own phone number, email address, wallet and computer workspace, so it can make calls, send emails and pay for things within permissions you set.

Cue's site gives examples such as booking appointments, emailing hotels, finding urgent care that takes your insurance, booking Taskrabbit help and comparing repair options. Agents can also work together in a group chat.
Cue does not publish prices on its site (checked 14 October 2026). Product Hunt lists it as having free options.

faq.q: Which devices does Cue run on?
faq.a: The site offers downloads for macOS and Windows and a mobile app.
A Product Hunt commenter said the app asked for an invite code at launch. Cue's site does not mention invites.

faq.q: How did Cue do on Product Hunt?
faq.a: It launched on 2 October 2026 and finished #11 for the day with 108 points and 4 comments.
